Rewritten sentence (concise, publishing-ready):
- "UPS Ground shipments sent from Los Angeles to San Francisco typically arrive within three business days; please check UPS's Time in Transit tool for an exact delivery estimate based on ZIP codes."

Verification summary:
- Official UPS guidance notes that a large majority of UPS Ground packages are delivered in three days or less, and it directs shippers to check transit times for specific shipments. ([ups.com](https://www.ups.com/us/en/support/shipping-support/shipping-services/domestic?utm_source=openai))
- UPS's rate & service documentation shows zone-based differences that affect transit time (so delivery between two California cities can vary by ZIP and zone). UPS therefore recommends using its Time in Transit lookup to confirm the exact window for a given origin/destination. ([ups.com](https://www.ups.com/assets/resources/webcontent/en_US/daily_rates.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Bottom line:
- The draft wording claiming "arrives within three business days" is generally aligned with UPS's official framing that most Ground packages are delivered within three days, but UPS does not guarantee the same window for every origin/destination — exact transit depends on ZIP codes and zones. To provide a definitive confirmation for a specific LA→SF route I can look up the Time in Transit result if you share the origin and destination ZIP codes (or I can run the UPS lookup for representative ZIPs).
